name: Can I build a pergola over 120 square feet without a permit?

mainEntity.name: If a pergola is freestanding, can it exceed 120 square feet and still avoid a permit?
mainEntity.text: If a pergola is freestanding, can it exceed 120 square feet and still avoid a permit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A freestanding pergola may seem simple, but size limits still matter. In the Los Angeles area, a detached structure over 120 square feet commonly falls outside the usual exemption and may need a permit. Even below that threshold, the project can still require review if it is attached to another structure, has a solid roof, includes lighting or fans, or sits near property lines. Homeowners should also check whether the pergola is being treated as a shade structure, patio cover, or accessory building, because different classifications can change the approval path. The safest approach is to verify the project’s exact dimensions and construction type before starting work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Usually no. Once a detached outdoor structure exceeds 120 square feet, it commonly triggers permit review in the Los Angeles area. Attachment, roof style, and utility connections can also create permit requirements even below that size.
